goal: Protect the public API from a single client exhausting it, without breaking the two integration partners who already burst well above the intended limit.

requirements.text: A request over the per-key limit is rejected with 429 and a Retry-After header saying when to try again.
An API key can be given a custom limit that overrides the default, so the two existing integration partners keep working unchanged.
Rate-limit counters survive an application restart, because restarting must not hand every client a fresh budget.

architecture: FastAPI service behind nginx. Redis is already in the stack for caching and is the intended counter store. Limits are per API key, read from an existing `api_keys` table that has no limit column yet.

# PRD: API rate limiting

## FR-1
A request over the per-key limit is rejected with 429 and a Retry-After header saying when to try again.

## FR-2
An API key can be given a custom limit that overrides the default, so the two existing integration partners keep working unchanged.

## CAP-1
Rate-limit counters survive an application restart, because restarting must not hand every client a fresh budget.

# Architecture

## counter-store
Redis is already in the stack and is the intended counter store.

## data-model
Limits are per API key, read from the existing `api_keys` table, which has no limit column yet.
